top_priorities: 1. Homepage (/index): remove the defensive apparatus (heading "A SYNTHESIS, NOT A CLAIM...", "What is not yet a universal guarantee", "Native is a foundation, not a browser claim", the three "not a claim that..." tails). Replace test-pass boasts with links to the live workbench. Keep one Status line: prototype, not on npm.

2. Benchmark page: rename internal gate language ("qualified", "Strict sample gate", "Not admitted", "Best median" cell text, R66 in headings). Move the "what is not measured" list into the methodology block. Drop the "compiler preview" and "honest" remarks. Keep every loss visible.

3. REPL chrome (35+ routes): collapse four empty-state messages into one or auto-initialise the scripted demo. Show the intro once, not twice ("Why this matters" duplicates). Fix /repl/snippet, which shows a raw SyntaxError. Say once per sync lab that it is a simulation.

4. Compare and /lib/*: delete meta paragraphs ("we do not win outright... honest near-tie", "Note the ordering on this page", "honest limit first", budget caveat repeated three times). Replace "spec v0.6" tags and status prose tails with a single status column. Remove adopter leaks ("What Hyper runs today") and internal names (Mextner, Danny).

5. Concepts and /learning: strip "Why it matters for us" plus R-number and § references, changelog voice ("now", "no longer", "earlier wording", "corrected"), card tags like "Compiler preview", and the whole "Runtime implementation and verification status" section on /learning.

6. Archival (/spec, /brief, /requirements, /decisions, /query-research corrections, /selectors-vs-datalog correction notice): move process history and changelogs out of the public nav or into a repository CHANGELOG. The public spec keeps the design, not the review trail.

7. Dead claims to fix rather than hedge: /effects "rewritten for you" (codemods unreleased), /init "6 of 17 choices are real" (use disabled controls), /api "no dedicated prose comment yet" (render nothing).
